lernapps.github.io.message:
feat(home): honest about quality, a way out for non-makers, no single authority

## Intent

Parents and teachers asked who vouches for the content and stumbled over the AI tutor and over the half of the home page meant for makers. Developers asked who decides on listing. The pages should be honest that a person stands behind each app, let readers report mistakes, and tie listing to rules instead of one person.

## Key changes

- Every app comes from a person; the platform helps to build it, but that is no guarantee. Mistakes in the content are reported on the app's page. This is said under the example apps and on /features/ as "Von Menschen gemacht".
- The AI tutor leaves the parents' card and the users' list; it is a feature of the explainer archetype, optional, and the app works without AI.
- After "Was du davon hast", a line tells everyone who does not build apps that they need not read on, with a link to the catalogue.
- The cost point says in plain words why it stays free; the technical detail stays on /features/.
- /features/: anyone can submit an app; it is checked against the rules for every app, which are exclusion criteria. The operator no longer appears as the one who decides. The thank-you is a prepared email that lernapps.net passes on.

## Dependencies and side effects

- The option "Fehler im Inhalt" on the app pages is in the apps repo (b24d521).

apps.message:
feat(app-page): "Fehler im Inhalt" as a feedback option on every app page

## Intent

Every app comes from a person; lernapps.net helps to build it but does not vouch for its content. Teachers, parents and learners who spot a mistake in the content need a way to report it.

## Key changes

- Every app page offers "Fehler im Inhalt" as a fifth feedback option. Like the others, it opens a prepared email.

## Dependencies and side effects

- The website says that mistakes are reported on the app's page (lernapps.github.io aaed045).
